messages:
maria: Hey infra — trying to request NVv4 quota increase for Azure Southeast Asia (southeastasia) but provisioning is blocked by account verification. Portal shows 'merchant verification required' and my payment card keeps failing 3DS. quota request stuck in Pending.

sam: ugh. Azure often wants company tax docs + legal entity verification. did finance upload W-8/W-9 or VAT number? also 3DS failures usually from issuer blocking corporate card for international auths.

vijay: I opened a support chat earlier. Support asked for: subscription id, company registration docs, and a signed tax form. They said merchant verification is separate from quota and must clear first. Ticket wants proof of payment method too.

alice: For short-term testing we can fall back to smaller GPUs (T4) in the same region or try NVv4 in another region where we already passed verification. But note that region change affects perf/cost and networking e2e tests.

maria: We don't have spare eastus2 quota, and moving region breaks benchmarking comparability. Also, even if quota gets approved, I'm seeing potential ENI/nic attachment limits in aseasia that will prevent scaling to >8 nodes.

network-eng: Confirmed — current NIC limit per subscription in southeastasia is 80. For our planned Dedicated pool we need ~200. I've opened NIC quota increase request (AZ-Q-1129), pending approval from Azure. This is separate from merchant verification.

jordan: Finance here — I can upload W-9 and company VAT info, but Azure is insisting the docs be attached to the subscription owner identity. Who is listed as the billing contact on this subscription? @maria or @jack?

maria: billing contact is @maria for this test subscription. Jordan can send files to me and I'll attach. But also the card 3DS issue: payment gateway rejects because of corporate issuer flags. We could switch to invoiced billing (pay-by-invoice) but that requires reseller onboarding.

jack: CSP/reseller route might be fastest. I've worked with a CSP partner who can onboard and provide invoice billing within 48–72h. It sidesteps 3DS because they invoice us. Need approval from finance to use CSP.

sam: If we do CSP, watch out: different subscription ids and limits; we'll need to migrate resources or re-provision. Not ideal for immediate load tests but fine for short-lived perf runs.

infra-bot: Ticket AZ-342112 created with Azure support (severity: high). Estimated initial response 24–72h. Reference: https://portal.azure.com/#supportrequest/AZ-342112

vijay: Action items: 1) @jordan upload tax docs (W-9 + VAT) and confirm billing contact. 2) @maria approve CSP onboarding if finance OK. 3) network-eng to push NIC quota request. 4) infra to keep AZ-342112 active and share updates. 5) use T4 fallback for perf smoke tests in the meantime.

jordan: On it — I'll upload the docs to the subscription billing contact and email the CSP contract template to @maria and @jack. Expect update by EOD. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks. if we don't have green by tomorrow morning we'll authorize CSP short-term spend and schedule perf runs. also, @network-eng pls confirm if private IP/route limits will need touching for the Dedicated pool.

network-eng: Will confirm NIC + private IP limits by EOD. If we need higher per-VNet IPs we'll include that in the same quota ticket.

jack: I'll prep the CSP onboarding checklist and estimate costs for invoice billing. If CSP approved, we can provision a small Dedicated NVv4 pool via partner within 2–3 days.

maria: Perfect. Keep this thread updated. If Azure support stalls, we'll escalate to account manager and open emergency CSP path.
